If it sounds like writing, rewrite it. (Read this: https://www.brainpickings.org/2013/08/21/elmore-leonard-10-rules-of-writing/)

Elmore Leonard’s 10 Rules of Writing – Brain Pickings
www.brainpickings.org
On July 16, 2001, Elmore Leonard (October 11, 1925–August 20, 2013) made his timeless contribution to the meta-literary canon in a short piece for The New York ...
LAKELAND, Fla. It was just an observation.

It was observed last week, when Tigers ace right-hander Justin Verlander was helping Angel Nesbitt with his inside pickoff move to second base. Nearly every morning, when Verlander warms up with Daniel Norris, giving the second-year lefty pointers on his curveball. And it was observed once again on Sunday afternoon, when Verlander stuck around after throwing live batting practice to watch some of the team’s younger pitchers.

LAKELAND, Fla. One day last week, Tigers ace right-hander Justin Verlander helped Angel Nesbitt with his inside pickoff move to second base. Nearly every morning, he warms up with Daniel Norris and gives the second-year lefty pointers on his curveball. And Sunday afternoon, he stuck around after throwing live batting practice to watch some of the team’s younger pitchers.
“A good observation,” said former Tigers pitching coach Jeff Jones, who has been helping in camp this spring.
“Yes,” manager Brad Ausmus said, Verlander has appeared to embrace more of a leadership role with this year’s Tigers.

“Everyone talks about growing as a player in terms of physical skills,” manager Brad Ausmus said. “But sometimes you grow as a player in the clubhouse as well and you realize you can take on more of a role in the team’s success, not only between the lines but in the clubhouse.”

Verlander is entering his 12th big league season. He has long been one of the team’s leaders, a face of the franchise. He was and one of a few guys that Ausmus leaned on down the stretch last season to keep the last-place Tigers playing the right way even when things weren’t going their way.

“I guess it just kind of comes with the territory when you’ve been around for a while,” Verlander said. “You’ve been through a lot. You’ve been through ups and downs. Whatever they need to work on or are working on, I’ve probably gone through it at some point.”
But that leadership hasn’t quite been on full display in years past as it has been this spring.

Maybe it’s the fact that Verlander is the unquestioned leader of the pitching staff — the most experienced pitcher and most accomplished pitcher. Last season, the Tigers had lefty David Price, whom Ausmus has called one of the best teammates he had’s seen. Perhaps Price’s presence rubbed off on Verlander.
Maybe the leadership is a reflection of where he is at on the mound. Last season, he battled through an early injury, then struggled in the first half before righting the ship in the second half.
But ask Verlander about it, and he’ll say nothing much has changed, that it has to do more with the pitchers he’s helping out these days.

“A few more younger starting pitchers that are willing to talk,” he said. “For years, it was kind of all the guys were pretty locked in, established. But it’s a little different now. I’ve made it clear to them if they have any questions, ask, or if they want to work on something.”

It’s still early in the spring, too early to talk about gut feels on where the Tigersteam will end up in the standings or predictions on how far they can go. But Verlander said there’s a definite “good vibe” around Tiger Town, “a really good feeling around the clubhouse.”

And a small part of that can certainly be chalked up to the way he’s taken the pitching staff under his wings, the observations his former pitching coach has made and what some of the Tigers’ young pitchers are saying.
“It’s been great,” Nesbitt said. “I feel like I can ask him anything.”
